sun.summary: The star at the center of our solar system, powered by nuclear fusion.
sun.description: The Sun is a ball of plasma held together by gravity. Its core fuses hydrogen into helium, releasing the energy that reaches Earth as light and heat.

facts.label: Rotation
facts.value: About 25 Earth days at the equator

mercury.summary: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun, with a cratered, rocky surface.
mercury.description: Mercury has almost no atmosphere to retain heat. Its surface experiences extreme temperature changes, and its elliptical orbit is the fastest of all the planets.

venus.summary: A rocky world with a thick atmosphere that traps heat, making it the hottest planet.
venus.description: Venus is similar in size to Earth, but its carbon-dioxide-rich atmosphere creates an intense greenhouse effect. It rotates in the opposite direction to most planets.

earth.summary: Our ocean-covered home, the only world known to support life.
earth.description: Earth has liquid water at the surface and an atmosphere rich in nitrogen and oxygen. Its tilted axis produces seasons as it travels around the Sun.

mars.summary: The red planet, colored by iron minerals that have rusted in its soil.
mars.description: Mars has a thin atmosphere, polar ice caps, and traces of ancient rivers and lakes. Its huge volcano Olympus Mons and canyon system Valles Marineris shape a dramatic landscape.

jupiter.summary: The largest planet, with bands of clouds and the immense Great Red Spot storm.
jupiter.description: Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium. Its clouds form contrasting belts and zones, while the Great Red Spot is a long-lived storm in its atmosphere.

saturn.summary: A giant planet surrounded by bright rings made mostly of ice, with rock and dust.
saturn.description: Saturn has no solid surface like Earth. Its ring particles range from tiny grains to large chunks, and its low average density is less than that of water.

uranus.summary: A pale blue-green world that rotates almost on its side.
uranus.description: Uranus has an extreme axial tilt of about 98 degrees. Methane in its atmosphere absorbs red light, helping give the planet its blue-green appearance.

neptune.summary: The most distant planet, with a blue atmosphere and powerful winds.
neptune.description: Neptune was located using mathematical predictions before direct observation confirmed it. Methane helps color its atmosphere, where storms and very fast winds develop.

pluto.summary: A small, icy world in the Kuiper Belt, beyond the eight planets.
pluto.description: Pluto has an elongated, tilted orbit and a thin atmosphere. Nitrogen ice covers parts of its surface, including the bright, heart-shaped region seen by New Horizons.
